answer.content: Fiber optic cable is a transmission medium that carries data as light through a glass or plastic core surrounded by cladding. Its advantages include very high bandwidth, low attenuation, immunity to electromagnetic interference, and security.  Fiber optic cable uses total internal reflection to keep the light confined within the core, ensuring minimal signal loss over long distances.  It is immune to electromagnetic interference, making it ideal for secure communication.  The core and cladding are typically made of glass or plastic, with glass being more durable and capable of higher bandwidth.  Installation requires skilled labor and can be expensive, but it is a reliable and secure option for data transmission.  Fiber optic cables are used in various applications, such as internet connections and telecommunications. [p. 1]
